Executive Summary & Architecture 2. Chapter 1: The "Indian" Model Layer (Sarvam Integration) 3. Chapter 2: The Core Engine (FastAPI + Twilio) 4. Chapter 3: The Workflow Engine (Logic & State) 5. Chapter 4: The Frontend Builder (React Flow) 6. Chapter 5: Post-Call Analytics (Oration Style) 7. Chapter 6: Deployment Strategy (Firebase & Cloud Run) 1. Executive Summary & Architecture This platform enables users to visually design voice agents (ElevenLabs style) that are specifically optimized for Indian languages (Hindi, Hinglish, Tamil, etc.) using Sarvam AI's models. High-Level Data Flow 1. Phone Call: Customer calls a Twilio number. 2. WebSocket: Twilio connects to our FastAPI backend via WebSocket. 3. STT (Ear): Incoming audio (Mulaw) is transcoded and sent to Sarvam Saaras (via WebSocket) for real-time transcription. 4. Brain: The Workflow Engine processes the text against the user-defined JSON graph. 5. TTS (Mouth): Response text is sent to Sarvam Bulbul V3 . 6. Output: Audio is played back to the caller. 7. Analysis: After the call, the transcript is sent to an LLM for "Oration-style" extraction (Sentiment, Intent, Action Items). Tech Stack ● Backend: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Websockets. ● Frontend: Next.js 14, React Flow, TailwindCSS, Shadcn UI. ● Database: Firestore (for storing agent configurations and call logs). ● Telephony: Twilio (Media Streams).

Chapter 1: The "Indian" Model Layer To build a robust system, we must not hardcode Sarvam. We use the Provider Pattern . This allows us to swap Sarvam for Deepgram or OpenAI later if needed, but defaults to Sarvam for now. 2.1 Abstract Base Classes Create a file app/services/ai_providers.py: from abc import ABC, abstractmethod from typing import AsyncGenerator, Optional class STTProvider(ABC): """Abstract Speech-to-Text Provider""" @abstractmethod async def connect(self): """Establish connection to the provider""" pass @abstractmethod async def send_audio(self, audio_chunk: bytes): """Send raw audio bytes""" pass @abstractmethod async def receive_text(self) -> AsyncGenerator[str, None]: """Yield transcribed text""" pass class TTSProvider(ABC): """Abstract Text-to-Speech Provider""" @abstractmethod async def generate_audio(self, text: str, voice_id: str, language: str) -> bytes: """Return audio bytes for the given text""" pass

We will use the synchronous REST API wrapped in async for simplicity in the first version. import aiohttp import base64 import os class SarvamTTS(TTSProvider): def __init__(self): self.api_key = os.getenv("SARVAM_API_KEY") self.url = "[https://api.sarvam.ai/text-to-speech](https://api.sarvam.ai/text-to-speech)" async def generate_audio(self, text: str, voice_id: str = "bulbul:v3", language: str = "hi-IN") -> bytes: payload = { "inputs": [text], "target_language_code": language, "speaker": "meera", # Example speaker "pitch": 0, "pace": 1.0, "loudness": 1.5, "speech_sample_rate": 8000, # Crucial for Telephony (Twilio) "enable_preprocessing": True, "model": "bulbul:v3" } headers = {"Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key": self.api_key, "Content-Type": "application/json"} async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session: async with session.post(self.url, json=payload, headers=headers) as response: if response.status != 200: error = await response.text() raise Exception(f"Sarvam TTS Error: {error}") data = await response.json() # Sarvam returns base64 audio audio_base64 = data["audios"][0] return base64.b64decode(audio_base64)
